chunks: Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was taken on the night journey, the time for salat arrived, so Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام gave the adhan.
So when he said, 'Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar,' the angels said, 'Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar.'
Then when he said, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,' the angels said, 'He has cast off all rivals.'
Then when he said, 'I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah,' the angels said, 'A Prophet has been sent.'
Then when he said, 'Come to salat,' the angels said, 'He has urged toward the worship of his Lord.'
Then when he said, 'Come to success,' the angels said, 'Successful is the one who follows him.'

key_terms.أُسْرِيَ: was taken on the night journey
key_terms.الْأَنْدَادَ: rivals or partners associated with Allah
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who responded to the adhan
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ: come to salat; the summons to prayer
key_terms.فَأَذَّنَ: he gave the adhan, the call to prayer

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the adhan during the Prophet’s night journey and the response of the angels?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the adhan given by Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام during the Miʿrāj of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, with the angels responding to each phrase. It highlights the theological meanings of tawhid, prophethood, and the call to salat and success.
